name: Error summary
summary: Use the Error summary at the top of a page to list validation errors and link each message to the field that needs attention.
whenToUse: Use after server-side or client-side validation fails on a page with user inputs.
Place it near the top of main content and repeat each error beside its field.
whenNotToUse: Do not use as the only indication that a field has an error.
Do not use for system failures or service-wide status messages; use an appropriate error page or notification instead.

anatomy.name: Summary container
anatomy.description: A GOV.UK JavaScript module contains an alert region.

anatomy.name: Title
anatomy.description: A heading identifies that the page contains a problem.

anatomy.name: Error list
anatomy.description: Each concise message links to the related input, fieldset legend or other appropriate target.

variants.name: Default
variants.use: Summarise one or more validation errors on the current page.

behaviour: Initialise the govuk-error-summary module so it can move focus to the summary when appropriate after validation.
Each link must target the relevant form control; for grouped controls, target the first control unless research supports a better focus target.
Keep server-side validation authoritative even when adding client-side validation.
accessibility: Put the summary inside main content and keep it visible in the document without JavaScript.
Use matching text in the summary and the inline error so users can connect them.
Do not rely on red colour or focus movement alone to announce errors.
content: Use a standard title such as “There is a problem”.
Write messages that explain what happened and how to fix it, without blaming the user.
Do not include the word “Error” before every list item.
